title: Cohomology models and retracts of complexes over a field
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $D(F)$ be the derived category of cochain complexes of $F$-vector spaces [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $H^i$ be its cohomology functors [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. A homotopy between chain maps $f,g:P\to Q$ means maps $h^i:P^i\to Q^{i-1}$ with $f-g=dh+hd$; a homotopy equivalence means chain maps inverse up to such homotopies. For any complex $P$, choosing vector-space complements $Z^i=B^i\oplus V^i$ and $P^i=Z^i\oplus T^i$, where $Z^i=\ker d^i$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$, gives a homotopy equivalence between $P$ and its zero-differential cohomology complex $H(P)$ with $H(P)^i=H^i(P)$. Every quasi-isomorphism of $F$-complexes is a homotopy equivalence, and the induced map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F)}(P,Q)\longrightarrow\prod_{i\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_F(H^i(P),H^i(Q))$$
is bijective. In particular every object of $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(F)$ [def-weil-point-fd-complexes] is isomorphic to a bounded finite-dimensional zero-differential complex and is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

Let $P$ be such an object and let $e:P\to P$ satisfy $e^2=e$. Then $e$ has a splitting $S\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{r}S$ in $D(F)$, with $ri=1_S$, $ir=e$, in which $S$ is represented by the zero-differential complex $\operatorname{im}H^i(e)$; the complementary summand is represented by $\ker H^i(e)$. If $v:P\to P$ commutes with $e$, then under this decomposition $ve$ acts as $rvi$ on $S$ and zero on the complementary summand. For two splittings $(S,i,r)$ and $(S',i',r')$ of the same $e$, the map $r'i:S\to S'$ is invertible with inverse $ri'$ and satisfies $(r'i)(rvi)=(r'vi')(r'i)$.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to write $Z^i=\ker d^i$, $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$ and $H^i(P)=Z^i/B^i$. The vector spaces $H^i(P)$ and $B^{i+1}$ are projective by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective]. Apply the lifting property of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] to the identity of each target of the surjections $Z^i\twoheadrightarrow H^i(P)$ and $d^i:P^i\twoheadrightarrow B^{i+1}$. It supplies linear sections $t_i$ and $s_i$. Set $V^i=t_i(H^i(P))$ and $T^i=s_i(B^{i+1})$. For $x\in P^i$, subtract $s_i(d^ix)$ to enter $Z^i$, then subtract $t_i$ of its quotient class to enter $B^i$. Applying $d^i$ and then the quotient proves uniqueness. Thus $P^i=B^i\oplus V^i\oplus T^i$, and $d^i:T^i\to B^{i+1}$ is an isomorphism. These choices are independent in each integer degree; no boundedness is used.

source.place: Tags 09FN (lemma-vector-space-is-free), 09FP (lemma-field-semi-simple); lifting formulation in algebra.tex, Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective)

proof.text: For any chosen complements in the statement, identify $V^i$ with $H^i(P)$ using the quotient. Let $a_P:H(P)\to P$ be inclusion of this block and $b_P:P\to H(P)$ its projection. They are chain maps with $b_Pa_P=1$. Define $h_P^i:P^i\to P^{i-1}$ as $(d^{i-1}|_{T^{i-1}})^{-1}$ on $B^i$ and zero on $V^i\oplus T^i$. For $x=b+v+t$, one has $d^{i-1}h_P^i(x)=b$ and $h_P^{i+1}d^i(x)=t$. Hence $dh_P+h_Pd=1-a_Pb_P$, the required homotopy. Inclusion sends a cohomology class to its chosen cycle, and projection sends a cycle to its class, so both induced cohomology maps are identities under [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor].

proof.text: If $f-g=dh+hd$ and $x$ is a cycle, then $(f-g)x=d(hx)$, a boundary. Thus homotopic maps induce the same cohomology maps, by the cycle formula of [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. For any chain map $f:P\to Q$, use the contractions of Step 2 on both complexes. Put $A_P=a_Pb_P$ and $A_Q=a_Qb_Q$. The degree $-1$ map $h_Qf+A_Qfh_P$ has $d(-)+(-)d=(1-A_Q)f+A_Qf(1-A_P)=f-A_QfA_P$. Thus $f$ is homotopic to $a_Q(b_Qfa_P)b_P$. The middle chain map between zero-differential complexes is exactly the degreewise map $H^i(f)$. In particular two maps inducing the same cohomology maps are homotopic.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism $f:P\to Q$, each $H^i(f)$ is invertible by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $u:H(Q)\to H(P)$ have components $H^i(f)^{-1}$ and put $g=a_Pub_Q$. The induced cohomology maps of $gf$ and $fg$ are identities, so Step 3 gives $gf\simeq1_P$ and $fg\simeq1_Q$. Conversely a homotopy equivalence induces inverse cohomology maps by Step 3. Consequently the images of all quasi-isomorphisms in the homotopy category $K(F)$ are already isomorphisms.

source.place: First sentence: transported perfect complexes and compatible idempotents; explicit field-complex argument

proof.text: Use the homotopy-category localization description in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and write $L:K(F)\to D(F)$ for its localization functor. By Step 4 the identity functor of $K(F)$ already inverts the specified arrows. The localization universal property therefore factors it as $R L\cong1_{K(F)}$ for a functor $R:D(F)\to K(F)$. Precomposing $L R$ with $L$ gives $L R L\cong L$, also the restriction of $1_{D(F)}$. The fully faithful part of the same universal property lifts this natural isomorphism and its inverse, giving $L R\cong1_{D(F)}$. Thus $L$ is an equivalence. This is just two applications of the defining localization property, and uses no boundedness or finite-dimensionality assumption.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category), localization at quasi-isomorphisms in the homotopy category

proof.text: A chain map $H(P)\to H(Q)$ is an arbitrary family of linear maps $H^i(P)\to H^i(Q)$, by the chain-map definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; both differentials are zero. A homotopy between two such maps forces their difference $dh+hd$ to be zero, so quotienting by homotopy identifies no distinct such families. Conjugating by $a_P,b_P,a_Q,b_Q$ in $K(F)$, then applying the equivalence of Step 5, gives the displayed bijection for derived Hom sets. Step 2 says these conjugating maps induce the identity on cohomology; hence this bijection is exactly the map induced by the functors of [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor], not merely an abstract bijection.

source.place: First sentence: transported perfect complexes and compatible idempotents; explicit field-complex argument

proof.text: If $P\in D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(F)$, [def-weil-point-fd-complexes] says its cohomology is finite-dimensional and supported in finitely many degrees. Thus Step 2 represents it by the bounded zero-differential complex $H(P)$. Each term is finitely generated, since the finite spanning condition of [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] is the module condition of [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and projective by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective]. This is precisely a bounded complex of finitely generated projectives, so $P$ is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

source.place: First sentence: transported perfect complexes and compatible idempotents; explicit field-complex argument

proof.text: Under Step 6, the idempotent $e$ is the family $E_i=H^i(e)$, with $E_i^2=E_i$ by functoriality [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. Write $S^i=\operatorname{im}E_i$ and $N^i=\ker E_i$ with zero differentials. The maps $x\mapsto(E_ix,(1-E_i)x)$ and $(s,n)\mapsto s+n$ are inverse: $E_i$ fixes its image, kills its kernel, and $E_i(1-E_i)=0$. They give an isomorphism of zero-differential complexes $H(P)\cong S\oplus N$. Finite spanning sets for $H^i(P)$ project under $E_i$ and $1-E_i$ to finite spanning sets for these summands; outside the cohomological support both are zero. Hence $S,N\in D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(F)$ by [def-weil-point-fd-complexes] and [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace].

source.place: First sentence: transported perfect complexes and compatible idempotents; explicit field-complex argument

proof.text: Transport the preceding degreewise inclusion $S\to H(P)$ and projection $H(P)\to S$ along the isomorphism $H(P)\cong P$ of Step 2. Call the resulting derived maps $i,r$. Their composites have cohomology $1_{S^j}$ and $E_j$ respectively, so the injectivity in Step 6 gives $ri=1_S$ and $ir=e$. Likewise the kernel summand gives the complementary summand of $P$. If $ve=ev$, functoriality of [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor] gives $H^j(v)E_j=E_jH^j(v)$. For $s=E_jx$, $H^j(v)s=E_jH^j(v)x$ lies in $S^j$; for $n\in\ker E_j$, $E_jH^j(v)n=H^j(v)E_jn=0$. Thus $H^j(v)$ preserves both summands. On their direct sum $H^j(ve)$ has blocks $H^j(v)|_{S^j}$ and zero. The first is $H^j(rvi)$; faithfulness from Step 6 gives the asserted block description in $D(F)$.

source.place: First sentence: transported perfect complexes and compatible idempotents; explicit field-complex argument

proof.text: Finally let $(S,i,r)$ and $(S',i',r')$ split the same $e$. All the following are formal compositions in the category of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. From $ir=i'r'=e$, $ri=1$ and $r'i'=1$ one gets $ei=i$, $ei'=i'$, $re=r$ and $r'e=r'$. Thus $(ri')(r'i)=r e i=ri=1_S$ and $(r'i)(ri')=r'e i'=r'i'=1_{S'}$. Moreover $(r'i)(rvi)=r'evi=r'vi$, whereas $(r'vi')(r'i)=r'vei=r'vi$. This proves the inverse formula and the requested intertwining equation, including for any other splitting not chosen from the cohomology model.
